rationale.usefulness: 7: The documented server and embedded modes, SDK routing checks, operation-to-test manifest workflow and explicit teardown boundaries make a bounded application pilot actionable. The educational specification/test/implementation exercise, website metadata workflow and video-job bookkeeping example are useful original applications with inspectable outputs. Each is conditional on actual API fidelity and explicitly unexecuted. No measured time savings or complete application compatibility justifies a higher score.
rationale.impact: 6: An AWS-published local API target with a public behavioral evaluation method is a meaningful advance for cloud-dependent agent development. It can give coding agents an additional feedback environment without provisioning real resources for every iteration. Evidence supports significance within that domain; there is no independently measured adoption, productivity gain, broad production equivalence or field-wide outcome. The autonomous construction account remains attributed to AWS.
rationale.novelty: 6: The distinctive documented combination is agent-built emulation guided by public API models and real-AWS-checked fidelity tests, with separate responsibilities for tests, issue finding and repairs. The report explains the feedback structure without treating promotional authorship claims as an audit. The sources do not establish that local cloud emulation itself is new or show comparative superiority, limiting the rating.
rationale.maturity: 5: Downloadable packages, substantial setup documentation, source access, explicit known-gap handling and release-specific fidelity reporting support practical trial use. Important limitations remain: strongest control-plane fidelity, varying data-plane and infrastructure-as-code coverage, ephemeral state, one account/Region per instance, no security-validation guarantee, no tested sustained-load readiness, and a costly source/embedded build. No installation or runtime exercise was performed for this report.
rationale.openness: 8: The archived README documents CC0 1.0 Universal with an Apache 2.0 vendor-directory exception, public source, public fidelity tests and opt-outs for default-on telemetry. The archived LICENSE contains the CC0 text and limitations. Portability through Linux packages and a user-built Docker image, plus reproducible scenario testing, are strong positives. Large build costs, cloud-dependent reference comparisons and refusal of external pull requests keep this below exceptional openness. Public emulator code is not evidence that underlying agent-model weights or all agent-development infrastructure are open.
rationale.sourceSupport: I independently checked the frozen report, evidence and rubric and verified their canonical hashes; all six unique supporting capture-file hashes also match. The November 11 launch is supported by dated publisher text explicitly saying launched/released today, while November 14 is the retrieval date. Undated guides remain undated. README and guides support fees, no-account use, platform routes, embedded-build cost, default telemetry and opt-outs. The report makes no unsupported current-version or universal compatibility claim and clearly discloses incomplete release-table coverage. Fidelity is correctly bounded by both emulator release and test-suite version. Security, IAM/policy, function-isolation, memory lifecycle and regional exclusions match the archived guides. The original use cases and proposed acceptance checks do not imply native execution, rendered media, independent benchmarking or real-cloud validation.
rationale.publication: The supplied 1924-word body is within 1800–2200 words for the 2000-word band associated with my independent impact score of 6. The coordinator must still apply the rubric to the final mean impact and compare the two independent ratings. I did not inspect another reviewer or worker opinion. No blocking factual or evidentiary correction is required for this bounded documentary report.
